newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq ends lower as Greenspan rattles investors.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq ends lower as Greenspan rattles investors.

text.p: Nasdaq stocks fell on Wednesday after Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan rattled investors with warnings about the surge in U.S. share prices and the risks of inflation.
The Nasdaq composite index shed 7.14 points, or 0.53 percent, to end at 1340.55. Losing issues led gainers 2639 to 1714.
"The market obviously showed some nervousness intraday. But the fact that it came back to end only slightly lower makes a good case for its strength," one trader said.

Dell Computer Corp resisted the market's slide, gaining 3-5/8 to 75-3/4 after releasing stronger-than-expected quarterly results. After the market closed Tuesday, Dell posted fourth-quarter earnings of $1.01 a share, topping analysts' estimates.
"Dell was the darling of the day for techs. Their gains would have been even higher if Greenspan hadn't rattled the market," one trader said.

Other big movers included Ortel Corp, which crumbled 8-1/8 to 12-1/2 after the company issued a caution on its results in the next two quarters. Etec Systems Inc shed 7-3/8 to 37-3/4 as the company pushed back the introduction of its Polyscan products.
